bahamas:diving.name: Bahamas
bahamas:diving.overview: Shark diving is the real specialty — Tiger Beach draws tiger sharks reliably from October through March, and oceanic whitetip sharks gather off Cat Island each spring. Blue holes (deep, flooded sinkholes, mostly in Andros) are the other signature feature, alongside generally calm, clear Caribbean water.
blurbs: Tiger sharks are at Tiger Beach in good numbers, and conditions overall are calm and clear — the best window of the year.

borabora:diving.name: French Polynesia
borabora:diving.overview: The Tuamotu atolls, Rangiroa and Fakarava above all, are drift dives through narrow passes where the tide brings in gray reef sharks, dolphins, eagle rays and, in season, hammerheads, mantas and a spawning gathering of groupers. The passes have strong current and suit experienced divers. Moorea, Tahiti and Bora Bora have calmer lagoon dives and snorkels with lemon sharks, rays and turtles, though some ray and shark tours feed the animals. Water holds 79 to 84°F all year, and the clearest months are May to October.
blurbs: Hammerhead sharks school in the Tiputa Pass at Rangiroa, at their best from January to March, with eagle rays in the same current. The water is at its warmest, about 84°F. It is the wet season, so rain can cloud the Society Islands more than the atolls.

Hammerheads are still gathering in the Tiputa Pass at Rangiroa, and gray reef sharks and eagle rays work the current alongside them. Water stays near 84°F, and the Tuamotu atolls get less rain than the Society Islands, so visibility holds up better there.

The last of the hammerhead season at Rangiroa, with gray reef sharks, dolphins and eagle rays still working the Tiputa Pass. Water is a warm 83°F and the atolls are calm and clear, with the rain easing in the Society Islands.

Rain is tapering off in the Society Islands and visibility there is variable, while the Tuamotu passes at Rangiroa and Fakarava stay good, with gray reef sharks in the current and dolphins in the Tiputa Pass in any month. A quieter month between the hammerheads and the dry-season peak.

The dry season brings the best visibility of the year to the atoll passes. Fakarava's South Pass holds hundreds of gray reef sharks facing the current, and Rangiroa has dolphins and eagle rays. The lagoons at Moorea and Bora Bora are calm and clear for snorkeling. Water is about 82°F, so a 3 mm wetsuit is enough.

Camouflage groupers gather to spawn in Fakarava's South Pass around the June full moon, and the gray reef sharks already holding the current feed on them. The current is strong and the dive suits experienced divers. Southeast winds can roughen the sea on the way out.

The grouper spawning in Fakarava's South Pass can still fill the channel with sharks around the July full moon, and manta rays begin to appear at Rangiroa. Humpback whales are in the waters around Moorea and Tahiti. This is the coolest water of the year, about 79°F, so a thicker wetsuit helps.

Manta rays visit Rangiroa's Tiputa Pass from late August, and humpback whales with calves are around Moorea, where regulated swims let snorkelers get in the water with them. Visibility is excellent and the seas are mostly calm.

The peak month for humpback whales around Moorea and Tahiti, with mothers and calves and regulated swims in the water for snorkelers. At Rangiroa, manta rays are in the pass, and Fakarava's passes stay clear and full of gray reef sharks. Water is about 79 to 80°F.
Humpbacks stay around Moorea through October, and manta rays at Rangiroa are seen through mid-October. The dry season is closing out, with clear water and good visibility in the passes.

The wet season sets in with more rain and some storm risk, and the whale season is over by early November. The Tuamotu atolls get less rain than the Society Islands, so the passes at Rangiroa and Fakarava are still worth diving, with gray reef sharks and dolphins.

Hammerhead sharks begin to return to the Tiputa Pass at Rangiroa, and the water warms toward 84°F. It is the wet season, with rain around the Society Islands, but the atoll passes keep good visibility.

Darwin and Wolf, the two legendary sites, are liveaboard-only and have the highest concentration of shark biomass recorded anywhere on Earth, with hammerhead schools numbering in the hundreds.

iceland:diving.name: Iceland
iceland:diving.overview: Silfra fissure — a crack between two tectonic plates filled with glacial meltwater so clear visibility can exceed 330 ft — is Iceland's genuinely unique dive site, cold enough to require a drysuit even in summer.
blurbs: Silfra stays open all winter, with the same 35 to 39°F water. A drysuit is essential and daylight is short, about 4 to 7 hours, so dive times are limited and wind chill can be harsh.

Manta ray and whale shark aggregations at sites like Hanifaru Bay are the marquee wildlife draw, on top of house-reef diving right off many resorts.

kaziranga:wildlifeViewing.name: Assam & Northeast India
kaziranga:wildlifeViewing.overview: Greater one-horned rhinos are virtually guaranteed on jeep safaris at Kaziranga, about four hours from Guwahati, which holds about two-thirds of the world's population. Wild elephants and wild water buffalo are also common, while tigers are seen only with luck. Hoollongapar, near Jorhat, is the best place for hoolock gibbons, India's only apes, with good chances on a quiet dawn walk.
blurbs: Burned patches open up Kaziranga's grassland and animals gather on the new shoots and ash, so rhinos, elephants and water buffalo are easy to see; tigers are elusive but sightings improve as cover drops.

Visibility is excellent where the grass has been burned and grazed low, making jeep safaris at Kaziranga very productive for rhinos, elephants and swamp deer, with better odds at a tiger than earlier in the season, still never certain.

Dry conditions gather rhinos, elephants and water buffalo around Kaziranga's remaining wetlands, and with the grass burned and grazed low, tiger sightings are likeliest now, though still a matter of luck. Manas burns its grass in March and April too, improving its visibility.

Last month before Kaziranga closes on 30 April: rhinos and elephants are concentrated at waterholes and tigers are most visible in short grass, but heat and humidity build and regrowth begins to cover sightlines.
Kaziranga is closed for the monsoon floods, and its rhinos, elephants and tigers retreat to the higher Karbi Anglong hills until the waters fall.

Ranges reopen in stages from late September, but tall post-monsoon elephant grass and waterlogged tracks hide most animals; rhinos and elephants are returning to the floodplain, and Pobitora reopens for its dense rhino population.

Controlled burning starts in the dry elephant grass this month, slowly improving sightlines at Kaziranga. Rhinos and water buffalo are reliably seen, elephants are frequently seen moving through the marshes, and tigers stay elusive in the remaining tall cover.

bagan:birding.name: Myanmar
bagan:birding.overview: Bagan's dry scrub holds four Myanmar endemics: White-throated Babbler, Burmese Bushlark, Hooded Treepie and the scarcer Jerdon's Minivet, with Mount Popa, about 90 minutes away, adding forest birds. Inle Lake holds over 20,000 migratory waterbirds from October to March, seen from boat tours.
blurbs: Cool, dry mornings suit Bagan's endemics (White-throated Babbler, Burmese Bushlark, Hooded Treepie, scarcer Jerdon's Minivet), and Inle Lake's wintering waterbirds, including Glossy Ibis and Brown-headed Gull, are seen on boat tours.

kaziranga:birding.overview: Kaziranga's prized, elusive targets are the Bengal Florican and Swamp Francolin; Great Hornbills are commonly seen, Pallas's Fish-Eagles frequent the wetlands and Bar-headed Geese winter. Manas, four to five hours from Guwahati, also holds the florican and Rufous-necked Hornbill; Nameri, explored on foot, is the best place for the White-winged Duck, a long shot.
blurbs: With the grass burned back, jeep safaris give their best chances at the elusive Bengal Florican and Swamp Francolin, while Bar-headed Geese and Spot-billed Pelicans fill the wetlands. Manas and Nameri are also open.
